isolation: Each scenario that needed its own data created a fresh catalog book (and, where needed, a matching stock-level record, address, or order) via the staff/shopper UI or a direct service call under a test actor's own token, then asserted only against that freshly created entity by id/title — never against the pre-seeded catalog or against entities left over from the prior validation run. Cross-shopper isolation scenarios used two distinct test accounts (test-shopper as Marco, test-shopper-two as Elena), each acting only on its own resources; Elena's cart/orders/addresses/notifications were confirmed empty before each isolation assertion.

Marco sees "Clean Architecture" with quantity 1 and a subtotal of "$29.99"
steps.observed: row shows Book="Clean Architecture" Quantity="1" Unit Price="$29.99" Line Total="$29.99" (all correct, computed client-side), but the page's "Subtotal" heading reads "Subtotal: $1.00" -- not $29.99. The underlying cause is in cart-service itself: GET /me/cart returns `"subtotal": 1`, i.e. the service is returning the item COUNT as the subtotal rather than a price-weighted total; the per-row Line Total is correct only because the frontend computes it independently from catalog price x quantity.

scenarios.scenario: A shopper cannot view every reservation

steps.text: an order holds a reservation for 1 copy of "Clean Architecture"
Marco is signed in as a Shopper
steps.command: signed in via IdP as test-shopper

steps.text: Marco tries to view every current reservation
steps.command: /staff/inventory route guard redirects Marco to /forbidden; no reservations view reachable, so attempted against the webapp's own API: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <marco>" http://.../api/inventory-service/reservations

steps.text: Marco is refused
steps.command: curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <marco>" http://.../api/inventory-service/reservations  vs.  curl -i http://.../api/inventory-service/reservations (no Authorization header at all)
steps.observed: both requests return byte-identical 401 responses (same status, same content-length:58, same body {"error":"Unauthorized","message":"Authentication failed"}). Marco's token is independently confirmed live in the same run (it reads/writes cart, orders, notifications, profile successfully around this same timestamp), so this is not a dead-token false negative -- but the gateway's 401 is, by design, indistinguishable between "no token", "expired token" and "valid token missing a scope". This 401 cannot be told apart from a request that never reached the app at all, so whether Marco was refused BY THE RULE (vs. by some unrelated gateway condition) cannot be settled from this evidence.

evidence.snapshot: Comparison probe: GET .../api/inventory-service/reservations with Marco's valid-but-unscoped bearer token -> HTTP/1.1 401, content-length 58, body {"error":"Unauthorized","message":"Authentication failed"}. The same GET with no Authorization header at all -> identical HTTP/1.1 401, identical content-length 58, identical body. The gateway gives no signal that distinguishes a correctly-enforced missing-scope refusal from an unauthenticated request never reaching the app.
